keyEvents.event: Nationalization of the oil industry and creation of PDVSA
keyEvents.impact: Oil rents became the foundation of the state and of every government's patronage system
Hundreds killed by security forces; discredited the two-party system and paved the way for Chavez

keyEvents.event: Hugo Chavez takes office and launches the Bolivarian Revolution
keyEvents.impact: New constitution, fusion of party, army and state, and a petro-financed alliance network (Cuba, ALBA)

keyEvents.event: Oil price collapse and onset of economic implosion under Maduro
keyEvents.impact: Hyperinflation, GDP lost roughly three quarters, and nearly 8 million Venezuelans emigrated

keyEvents.event: Guaido interim presidency recognized by the US and ~50 states; US oil sanctions
keyEvents.impact: Dual-power standoff failed as the armed forces stayed loyal; sanctions deepened dependence on Russia, China and Iran

keyEvents.event: Disputed presidential election: Maduro declared winner despite opposition tally sheets showing a Gonzalez victory
keyEvents.impact: Mass repression, Gonzalez exiled; Machado became the face of the opposition and won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize

keyEvents.event: US naval buildup in the Caribbean and lethal strikes on alleged drug boats from September
keyEvents.impact: Washington framed the regime as a narco-terrorist 'Cartel de los Soles' and prepared the ground for force

keyEvents.event: US raid captures Maduro in Caracas (3 January); Delcy Rodriguez sworn in as acting president
keyEvents.impact: Chavista apparatus survived under US tutelage: oil sector opened to foreign firms, US embassy reopened, amnesty law, but no election date

history.narrative: A petro-state hollowed out by a decade of collapse whose revolutionary leadership was decapitated by a US raid but not replaced. The surviving chavista elite now trades oil access and cooperation with Washington for survival, while a popular opposition waits for elections that keep receding.

redLines.description: Forced handover of power to the opposition or prosecution of the remaining chavista leadership
Large-scale US ground occupation or seizure of oil fields without a negotiated deal
Reimposition of a full oil embargo cutting the last source of hard currency

internalDivisions.name: Chavista establishment vs. democratic opposition (Machado/Gonzalez) demanding elections
Rodriguez pragmatists vs. hardline security chiefs and colectivos wary of US deals
Lawless mining arc and border zones held by ELN, gangs and Tren de Aragua

goals.description: Preserve the chavista state apparatus and its leaders' immunity through the US-managed transition
Trade oil access for sanctions relief and restore production with foreign investment
Delay and shape elections to avoid a decisive opposition victory
Keep the armed forces cohesive and contain armed groups in the mining and border regions
